givens: Strip width 4 cm and original straight length 13 cm
P and Q are the two exposed rectangles
x is only the exposed P length, not the turn diagonal
proof: Let y be the exposed length of Q. Both P and Q have the unchanged strip width 4.

The 45-degree crease turns the original strip axis by 90 degrees. The two parallel original long edges meet the crease at longitudinal coordinates separated by 4, since cot(45 degrees)=1. Thus the diagonal transition consumes 4 cm of original strip length.
The original material-length decomposition is x+4+y=13, independent of the doubled-layer triangular overlap.
P=4x=2Q=8y implies x=2y. Thus x+y=9, y=3, x=6 uniquely, C.
The turn diagonal has length sqrt(4^2+4^2)=4sqrt(2), E, but is a distinct segment from x.
